answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted random committees. Each agent locks collateral in a vault to join a rotating beacon that assigns verification duties; that locked stake is an island of value slashed whenever the agent double-signs. Because committee selection is unpredictable, an attacker cannot win merely by spawning countless fake identities. To bias even a single round they must own a large share of the entire vault, so the attack cost scales with total staked value rather than with the number of Sybils created.
